Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE4703 : Steel Structures Design Practice { 0-0-2 / 1}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Session 1: Structural Steel Design Principles (2 hours)
Session 2: Connection Design – Bolts and Welds (2 hours)
Session 3: Connection Design – Gusset Plates and Brackets (2 hours)
Session 4: Design of Tension Members (2 hours)
Session 5: Design of Compression Members (2 hours)
Session 6: Design of Anchor Bolts and Base Plates (2 hours)
Session 7: Design of Beams and Flexural-Torsional Buckling (2 hours)
Session 8: Design of Plate Girders (2 hours)
Session 9: Design of Beam-Columns (2 hours)
Session 10: Practical Case Studies and Review (2 hours)

Course Objective

1 .

Provide hands-on experience in designing structural steel components and connections using design specifications and codes.
2 .

Enhance students’ ability to apply limit state design principles to real-world structural steel projects.
3 .

Develop problem-solving skills through practical design assignments in a studio environment.
4 .

Prepare students to integrate theoretical knowledge with practical applications in steel structure design.

Course Outcome

1 .

(1) Apply limit state design principles to analyze and design various steel structural components.
(2) Design and detail bolted, welded, shear, and moment connections, ensuring structural integrity.
(3) Develop practical competency in using IS 800:2007 and other relevant design codes for steel structures.
(4) Evaluate stability and failure modes of steel members, including beams, columns, and plate girders.
(5) Produce professional-quality design documentation that includes calculations, sketches, and design reports for real-world applications.

6462.t: CE6334: Evaluation and Strengthening of Pavements
6462.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE6334 : Evaluation and Strengthening of Pavements { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1 [6 hours]
Introduction to Pavement Evaluation: Purpose of pavement evaluation, Different types of pavement, Selection of appropriate type of pavements, Critical factors for each type, Functions and purpose for various layers, Pavement deterioration pattern, Cost and economics of pavement construction, Repair and rehabilitation.
Module II [6 hours]
Purpose of Pavement Evaluation, Types of evaluation – functional and structural assessment, Classification of Different types of Evaluation, Pavement Inventory, Concept of Serviceability, Pavement Serviceability Index, Pavement Serviceability Rating, Critical threshold for different pavement types
Module III [6 hours]
Pavement Roughness Measurement, Purposes, Factor influencing roughness, Limitations, Classification of roughness measuring system, International Road Roughness Experiment, Concept of International Roughness Index (IRI), Various models for evaluating IRI and operating principle, Contact type Equipment, Non-contact type equipment, Advantages and disadvantages.
Module IV [6 hours]
Frictional Evaluation, Purposes, Friction Indices, Measurement of longitudinal and lateral friction, Concept of slip and friction coefficient, Factors affecting surface friction, Spot and continuous friction measuring system, significance and limitations, Concept of Fixed and variable slip ratio for friction measurement.
Module V [6 hours]
Overlay design of pavement, Concept of Benkelman Beam method as per IRC: 81, Deflection measurement, Corrections, advantages and limitations, Concept of Falling Weight Deflectometer as per IRC 115, Deflection bowl characteristics, Analysis of FWD results, Pavement condition survey, Corrections, Determination of overlay thickness, Economic assessment.
Module VI [6 hours]
Evaluation of pavement materials – Labs and Field, selection of homogenous sections, Destructive and non-destructive tests, Identification of distresses and their severities, Causes for distresses, Appropriate maintenance strategies for distresses, Case studies.

Course Objective

1 .

Understand the purpose and methods of pavement evaluation and relevant concepts.
2 .

Learn various roughness measurement techniques for pavement condition survey
3 .

Gain knowledge of frictional evaluation methods for various pavement types
4 .

Familiar with overlay design methods and economic viability.

Course Outcome

1 .

After the completion of this course, students will be able to:
CO1: Understand both flexible and rigid pavement maintenance concepts
CO2:Design overlays by different methods
CO3: Acquire data sets required to assess the performance of pavement
CO4: Plan Road maintenance activities for structural and functional evaluation
CO5: Understand the concept of distress and find out the root causes

Essential Reading

1 .

R Srinivasa Kumar, Pavement Evaluation Maintenance Management System, Universities Press , First Edition

2 .

Yang,, Design of Functional Pavement,, Mc. Graw Hill, , Latest Edition

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Relevant Latest IRC and other Codes and Specifications., IRC codes, IRC , New Delhi

2 .

D. Croney & P. Croney,, The Design and Performance of Road Pavements,, McGraw Hill Professional, , Latest Edition.

Journal and Conferences

1 .

Transportation Research Board, Washington D.C.
2 .

World Conferences on Transportation Research

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE6601 : Modern Construction Materials { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Concrete as Construction Material & Concrete Making Materials (8 hours):
Constituent materials, Cement production, composition, and classifications, Supplementary cementing materials, Microstructure of cement hydrates, Aggregate classifications, Alkali Aggregate reactions, Mineral Admixtures and classifications, Chemical admixtures and classifications, working mechanisms of admixtures.
Module 2 :

Properties of Fresh and Hardened Concrete (8 hours)
Production of concrete, Ready mix concrete, Pumping of concrete, Steps of concreting, Fresh concrete, workability and its measure, Mechanical and elastic properties of concrete, Mix design of concrete, Factors affecting the properties of concrete, Shrinkage and creep, Durability of concrete and its measurement, Applications of Fibre Reinforced Concrete, Self-Compacting Concrete, Alternate Concrete materials on high performance and High Strength.
Module 3 :

Special Concretes (6 hours)
Properties and Advantages of High Strength and High-Performance Concrete, Properties and Applications of Fibre Reinforced Concrete, Self-Compacting Concrete, Alternate Concrete materials on high performance and High Strength.
Module 4 :

Metals (6 hours)
Types of Steel, The Manufacturing Process of Steel, Advantages of New Alloy Steel, Properties and Advantages of Aluminum and Its Products, Types of Coatings and Coatings to Reinforcement, Applications of Coatings.
Module 5 :

Composites (8 hours)
Types of Plastics, Properties & Manufacturing process, Advantages of Reinforced polymers, Types of F.R.P., F.R.P. on different structural elements, Applications of F.R.P., Types and properties of Water Proofing Compounds, Non-weathering Materials, Flooring, and Facade Materials and their uses, Types and Differences between Smart and Intelligent Materials, Case studies showing the applications of smart & Intelligent Materials.

Course Objective

1 .

To understand the function and effects of cement, aggregate, and admixture in concrete and their properties
2 .

To understand concrete as a material and its properties.
3 .

To understand the norms and their basis in codes for mix design and quality assessment of concrete and its constituents.
4 .

To study and understand the properties of modern construction materials such as special concretes, metals, composites, water-proofing compounds, non-weathering materials, and smart materials

Course Outcome

1 .

It will help students understand the basic principles of concrete science and engineering.
2 .

The students will learn about mix design, the assessment process of concrete quality, common concrete issues, and the possible mitigation methodologies in the field as an engineer.
3 .

The students will learn about the preparation and utilization of high-performance concrete in construction.
4 .

The students will be able to efficiently identify the utilization of various metals in the construction field.
5 .

The students will be able to apply their knowledge of polymer composites, different flooring materials, façade materials, and smart materials in construction.

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Thermal analysis (TG, DTA, DSC, Dilatometer): Thermal analysis methods- principles, instrumentation, data analysis, factors affecting thermal analysis curves, and applications in ceramics, derivative thermogravimetry, self-generated thermogravimetry, thermo dilatometry.

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EC4720 : Microwave Engineering Laboratory { 0-0-2 / 1}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

[1] Study the characteristics of different microwave components.
[2] Study the characteristics of the waveguide using the Reflex Klystron based microwave test bench.
[3] To measure the fundamental frequency of a rectangular waveguide.
[4] To Study V-I characteristics of Gunn Diode and determination of SWR and reflection coefficient using Gunn Oscillator based microwave test bench.
[5] Measurement of S-parameter and input/output power in E-Plane and H-plane Tee.
[6] Study of the Magic Tee.
[7] Study of Circulator.
[8] Study of Directional Coupler.
[9] Measurement of the Radiation pattern of a Horn Antenna
[10] Design and simulation of microstrip patch antenna using CST Microwave studio suite.
[11] Design and simulation of microstrip patch antenna structure using HFSS.
[12] Introduction to Vector Network Analyzer (VNA).

1 .

Students will be able to study various Microwave components and measure their parameters using Klystron/Gunn Oscillator

Students will be able to measure the VSWR, reflection coefficient, frequency, wavelength and impedance using a microwave test bench
3 .

Students will be able to study the characteristics of Directional Coupler and magic tee. Besides, they will be able to measure the radiation pattern of a horn antennas.
4 .

Students will be able to design and simulate a simple microstrip patch antenna structure using CST Microwave studio and HFSS. Besides, they will also learn teh uses of VNA (or Performance Network Analyzer (PNA)).

Course Outcome

1 .

After the completion of this course, students will be able to:
CO1: understand the design aspect of Power dividers, Couplers, and feed networks using HFSS
CO2: describe describe the working principle of Power dividers, Couplers, and feed networks qualitatively.
CO3: analyze different parameters using experiments and electromagnetic simulator HFSS.
CO4: apply the knowledge to investigate the cause and effect qualitatively
CO5: construct/design some basic design by their own

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : ID4304 : Rapid Product Development Technologies { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Overview of Rapid Product Development: Product Developing Cycle, Components of RPD, Classification of manufacturing processes
Preprocessing: Solid Modeling, Data exchange formats, STL file format, RP Preprocessing
Rapid Prototyping (RP): Introduction to RP, Need of RP Basic Principles of RP, Steps in RP, Process chain in RP in integrated CAD-CAM environment, Advantages of RP, Classifications of different RP techniques, Selection of RP processes, Issues in RP, Emerging trends
RP Techniques: Solid RP, liquid RP techniques and Powder RP Techniques -Process Technology and Comparative study of Selective laser sintering, Selective powder binding, etc.
Rapid Tooling (RT): Introduction to RT, Indirect RT processes –silicon rubber molding, epoxy tooling, spray metal tooling and investment casting. Direct RT processes –laminated tooling, powder metallurgy based technologies, welding based technologies, direct pattern making, emerging trends in RT
Reverse Engineering: Geometric data acquisition, 3D reconstruction
Applications and case studies: Engineering applications, Medical applications

Course Objective

1 .

The course addresses the fundamentals of methods and techniques to support engineering design processes, by focusing on the opportunities provided by Reverse Engineering, Rapid Prototyping and Rapid Manufacturing

Course Outcome

1 .

Knowledge and understanding
Students will
i. acquire basic knowledge about the main opportunities provided by Reverse Engineering and Rapid Prototyping tools, which represents an opportunity to learn how to conduct detailed product design by benefitting from cutting-edge technologies
ii. understand the main differences, pros and cons of the alternative technologies to carry out design tasks supported by 3D-printing devices
iii. acquire knowledge about some important Additive Manufacturing processes used for the fabrication of prototypes and components
iv. be able to identify the advantages and limitations of Reverse Engineering and Additive Manufacturing processes in the overall context of design, manufacturing and industrial design

19262.t: MA5305: Integral Equations and Integral Tranforms
19262.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : MA5305 : Integral Equations and Integral Tranforms { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introduction to Integral Equations, classification: Volterra and Fredholm integral equations,
First kind, second kind, Relation between differential and integral equations, Conversion of initial and boundary value problems into integral equations
Module 2 :

Fredholm Integral Equations, Fredholm equations of the second kind, terative method (successive approximations)
Volterra integral equations of the first and second kinds, Successive approximation and resolvent kernel for Volterra equations
Module 3 :

Laplace transform: definition, properties, Inverse Laplace transform,
Applications to solving ordinary differential equations Convolution theorem, Integral equations solved by Laplace transforms
Module 4 :

Fourier transform and its properties, Fourier sine and cosine transforms, Applications of Fourier transforms in solving PDEs and integral equations
Module 5 :

Other Integral Transforms, Hankel Transform, Mellin Transform, Z-Transform (brief introduction), Applications to simple models in physics and engineering

Course Objective

1 .

Understand the formulation and classification of integral equations.
2 .

Learn methods to solve various types of integral equations.
3 .

Study important integral transforms (Fourier, Laplace, Z-Transform, Hankel, etc.) and their applications.
4 .

Apply transforms to solve differential and integral equations.

Course Outcome

1 .

Classify and analyze different types of integral equations (Fredholm, Volterra, first kind, second kind, homogeneous, nonhomogeneous).
2 .

Demonstrate problem-solving skills in both theoretical and application-oriented contexts involving integral transforms and equations.

Essential Reading

1 .

A.M. Davie, Integral Equations and Their Applications, Wit Press

2 .

Sneddon, The Use of Integral Transforms, McGraw-Hill Inc

A.J. Jerri, Introduction to Integral Equations with Applications, Wiley–Blackwell

2 .

Debnath and Bhatta , Integral Transforms and Their Applications, Chapman and Hall/CRC

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : MM3122 : Heat Treatment Laboratory { 0-0-2 / 1}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introduction to Heat Treatment Laboratory: Safety instructions, Muffle furnace, salt bath furnace, quenching tanks, metallurgical microscope, hardness tester
Module 2 :

Annealing of Carbon Steels: Annealing of low, medium, and high carbon steels, Metallography and hardness testing, Microstructural evolution with carbon content
Module 3 :

Normalizing of Steels: Normalizing of low, medium and high carbon steels, Metallography and hardness testing
Module 4 :

Quenching of Steels: water quenching of medium and high carbon steels, Martensite formation and hardness analysis, Crack sensitivity and internal stresses
Module 5 :

Tempering of Quenched Steels: Tempering at different temperatures, Hardness reduction, Tempered martensite structure
Module 6 :

Cold Work and Recovery in Pure Copper: Cold rolling of pure copper, Metallography and hardness testing, Discussion on recovery and recrystallization
Module 7 :

Carburization of Low Carbon Steel: Pack carburizing process, Case depth and surface hardening, Microstructure of carburized and core regions

Course Objective

1 .

To familiarize students with the fundamental principles and procedures of heat treatment processes.
2 .

To develop the ability to analyze microstructure and hardness variations due to different heat treatments.

Course Outcome

1 .

Identify the different heat treatment processes and demonstrate safe handling of lab equipment such as furnaces, quenching media, and hardness testers.
2 .

Analyze the microstructure and hardness of low-, medium-, and high-carbon steels subjected to annealing and normalizing, and correlate with their carbon content.
3 .

Evaluate the effect of quenching on the hardness and microstructure of medium- and high-carbon steels.
4 .

Interpret the microstructural changes and property improvements due to tempering of quenched steels.
5 .

Examine the influence of cold working and annealing on pure copper.

6 .

Assess surface hardening achieved through carburization in low-carbon steels.

Essential Reading

1 .

Vijendra Singh, Physical Metallurgy, Standard publisher

Supplementary Reading

1 .

T.V. Rajan, Heat treatment: principles and techniques, Standard publisher

Journal and Conferences

1 .

Heat treatment and surface engineering
